summary: compat-os fix round: I confirmed and fixed all 19 review findings, each with regression tests. Both YAML suites stay at baseline: roll-os 1455/0/51 and ES 3809/1/95, with 0 regressions in either. Two new REST fixtures were captured and pass: os_fixes_r4.json (363 steps, fresh OpenSearch 3.9.0) and es_sortmix_meta.json (124 steps, private ES 9.5.5). The whole rest_fixtures run is green, os_ism.json included. Two parts are only approximate: the order of docvalue_fields wildcards over metadata fields (ES '_*' differs), and the ISM explain order for explicit index lists.
public_api:
search-codec: SegmentReader::uninverted_bytes(field) -> usize (memory of the built UNINVERTED values, 0 before first use). Uninverted ordinals are now u32.
search-es opensearch::ism: pub fn reconcile(prev: &ClusterState, next: &mut ClusterState, now: i64), called by Cluster::update on every OpenSearch-dialect state change. It replaces the create/delete hooks: on_index_created is private now, and api::indices no longer calls ISM.
search::sort: pub fn merge_widening(&[&[ValueFormat]], &[Sort]) -> EsResult<Vec<usize>>, merge_values, widen_values, widen_formats, merge_cast_failure.
search::id_fielddata::scripts(&ClusterState) -> bool.
scripts::DocHost::with_id_fielddata(bool).
meta::data_streams::backing_index_name has no date in the OpenSearch dialect.
search/mod.rs check_unsigned_sort_mix(&[&[ValueFormat]]) now runs in both dialects.
done:
#1 numeric_type long/date on floating fields (sort.rs):
- field_format returns Long; rescale truncates Double/Float to long; parse_after reads long bounds; sort_type_name says LONG
- numeric_type double on float fields gives a Double format
- reduce (search/mod.rs): own_formats is computed before the merge; merge_values turns scaled_float and Double-format values into doubles, which fixes long-vs-scaled_float merge order in both dialects
- ES SortFieldValidation: mixed numeric types with a float or double widen to doubles, other mixes fail with 'incompatible sort types [A] and [B]'
- OS: keyword/number mixes fail with a 500 class_cast_exception
- OS date_nanos missing values keep Long.MIN

#2 _id fielddata setting: aggregation scripts (Values, Scripted), runtime fields (Evaluator) and painless_execute use DocHost::with_id_fielddata(id_fielddata::scripts(st)). The request-cache key carries the flag only for field uses (a cached script aggregation keeps answering, as in OS). OS errors carry IdFieldMapper frames: scripting.rs drops the ES lookup frames when OS frames are present.

#3/#4 ISM: reconcile runs in Cluster::update and diffs index uuids. Resize, restore, rollover, data stream create/delete and every other path now manage and release indices. Templates apply only to indices created after their last_updated_time (as findMatchingPolicy does). '.'-prefixed indices count as hidden.
#5 restricted_index_pattern (setting or the default config index) applies to auto-management and add(). add() lists those failures first.

#6 template overlap uses an automaton intersection (globs_intersect DP). findSelfConflictingTemplates is added. A refused policy still creates the config index (checkAndUpdateIMConfigIndex), as in OS.
#7 validateFormat (#, :, _, invalid chars, exclusion content, at least one inclusion). Exclusion patterns are honoured.

#8 explain-all:
- size/from/sortField/sortOrder/queryString, with total counting every match
- sort on mapped config fields, with search_phase_execution_exception for unknown or text fields
- explicit lists: from>0 gives the result-window error; queryString narrowing
- expand_wildcards removed from spec/opensearch/plugins/ism.explain.json

#9 get policies:
- queryString is a query_string over the policy id keyword (case-sensitive, AND/OR/NOT, * and ?)
- paramAsInt / negative / SortOrder enum / no-mapping errors
- ties keep config-document order (seq_no)

#10 action validations:
- notification, snapshot (fields), index_priority, shrink (exactly one option, ranges), convert_index_to_remote (fields, defaults), alias (init checks), search_only parameterless, retry count required, replica_count/force_merge ranges, transform/rollup required
- allocation maps stringify values, and arrays/objects fail with 500 'Can't get text on a START_ARRAY'
- change_policy body parser (Invalid field ... ChangePolicy, include filters)
- policy version tombstones within gc_deletes (60s)

#11 OS data stream backing index names have no date. OS rollover responses have no 'lazy'. OS SnapshotInfo has no repository or feature_states and adds remote_store_index_shallow_copy, with OS version id/version. OS GET _snapshot has no total/remaining.
#12 OS fields API skips metadata fields (fields.rs check_internal/metadata_requests).
#13 OS filter_path exclusions drop the containers they partially matched when they end up empty (xcontent/filter.rs).
#14 OS field sort refuses 'format' (search_source.rs).
#15 the unsigned_long mix check runs in both dialects.

#16 ES: script_fields keep _id under stored_fields _none_. top_hits with stored_fields _none_ drops _id (ES and OS). OS: stored_fields _none_ with a requested _source gives the shard 500 search_exception.
#17 collapse on _data_stream_timestamp gives the type message in both dialects.

#18 _id fielddata:
- shows in _stats/_cat fielddata (engine load_fielddata/field_stats_into using uninverted_bytes), only when the setting allows it
- _cache/clear?fielddata releases it from the stats
- uninvert uses u32 ordinals with an overflow guard

#19 docvalue_fields metadata fields:
- a per-dialect table of which metadata fields load fielddata (ES: _tier/_ignored_source/_field_names/... fail; OS: _ignored/_version fail)
- wildcards reach metadata fields in Java HashSet order: the first one without fielddata fails, the others answer
- explicit _index and ES _index_mode answer

Unit tests:
- opensearch::ism: overlap automaton, exclusions/wildcards, query strings, validateFormat/self-conflict, action validations
- search::sort: widening, merge values, numeric_type long
- xcontent::filter: OS empty containers
- meta::data_streams: OS backing name
- search-codec segment test: uninverted_bytes

Docs:
- compatibility.md: ISM, sort mixing, filter_path/fields/sort-format notes
- contracts.md: uninverted_bytes, ism::reconcile
remaining: docvalue_fields wildcards over metadata fields: the first failing field follows a Java HashSet order model. ES '_*' reports _id where roll reports _routing, because the ES matched set is larger or ordered differently. Explicit metadata names all match.
_id fielddata has no fielddata circuit breaker. _cache/clear only resets the stats: the uninverted values stay cached in the segment reader for its life.

ISM:
- policies are still never executed (explain has no state/action/info, retry reports 'no metadata')
- explain over explicit index lists and wildcards orders entries like a uuid-keyed HashMap that roll can't reproduce
- POST explain filter bodies (ExplainFilter) are not parsed
- the seq_no model's asynchronous write order is only approximate when steps don't wait
The OS SnapshotInfo shape change is verified by diff only. No fixture covers it, because the rest_fixtures cluster has no path.repo (fs repositories need a node setting there).
Earlier items still open: verbose_pipeline, trained k-NN models, hybrid collapse scoring, k-NN stats fetch counts, derived text fields not analyzed.

notes_for_others: durability / everyone: Cluster::update now calls opensearch::ism::reconcile(prev, next) in the OpenSearch dialect. It returns early when no ISM policies or managed indices exist, so it costs nothing otherwise. Don't call ISM hooks from APIs any more.

compat-es / perf: the search reduce now builds every index's sort formats before merging. merge_values converts scaled_float and Double-format values to doubles for cross-index comparison. ES widening rewrites values and formats for mixed numeric keys.

compat-es: docvalue_fields refuses more metadata fields explicitly (ES: _tier, _ignored_source, _field_names, _data_stream_timestamp, _nested_path, _feature). The fields API path maps _tier to nothing, so it doesn't hit the new error.
search-painless: OpenSearch-dialect host errors that carry org.opensearch frames now have the interpreter's ES lookup frames stripped in scripting::from_json_error.

Whoever owns ingest/processors.rs and search/runtime_query.rs: their lib tests don't compile (Result<Vec<String>,String> used as a Vec; Predicate::matches is private), which blocks `cargo test -p search-es --lib` for everyone.

Step files and tools are in ~/.cache/roll-search/compat-os/gen/ (os_all.txt, es_all.txt, ism_*.txt; diff.py/show.py/txt2fixture.py support [sleep N] prefixes, and DIALECT=elasticsearch for ES fixtures). The private containers roll-os-compat-os-ref (19556) and roll-es-compat-os (19557) are stopped. roll-es-ref was not used.
